# Implementation Plan: In-flight cancellation/abort for the `/remote on` self-onboard device-flow poll
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-autoconnect-interactive-self-onboard-remote-on"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-26. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-autoconnect-interactive-self-onboard-remote-on/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The interactive `/remote on` self-onboard (GitHub device flow → write `~/.happy` creds → attach) is
**already shipped** on codex main (wrapper `5f9dc1105e` / inner `527027282e`, US-009 + US-002/003/004;
patch-surface invariants 59 + 60). The one remaining gap, scoped by the operator to **OPTION A**, is
**in-flight cancellation**: `/remote on` spawns `remote_on_flow` fire-and-forget
(`slash_dispatch.rs:837`, no `JoinHandle`/`CancellationToken` retained), so issuing `/remote off`
while the device-flow poll is in flight does **not** stop the poll — it runs until the grant is
approved or the device code expires (commonly ~900 s).

This plan adds cooperative cancellation: an overlay-owned cancel handle threaded into
`run_self_onboard`/`poll_for_token` that returns a new `OnboardError::Cancelled` promptly, a
`ChatWidget` field holding that handle, a `.cancel()` call on `/remote off`, a hermetic abort-path
test, cleanup of the stale code comment, and a patch-surface invariant row. ~1–2 small, mostly
overlay-local stories; zero new feature flags; zero new runtime dependencies.

### Technical Constraints
- **Dependency asymmetry (informs the design):** `codex-happy` (Cargo.toml:36) has tokio
  `["time","sync","rt","macros","net"]` — so `tokio::sync::watch` is available to the overlay. The
  `tui` crate's own tokio features (Cargo.toml:104-112) do NOT list `sync`, and its `tokio-util` dep
  (line 128) enables only `["time"]` — **but** the tui crate already uses `tokio::sync::mpsc` (e.g.
  in `chatwidget.rs`, `app.rs`, `app_event_sender.rs`) because Cargo **feature unification** turns on
  tokio `sync` workspace-wide (codex-happy and others enable it; `tokio-stream` also pulls `sync`). So
  `tokio::sync` IS usable in tui builds in practice — the earlier "TUI cannot name tokio::sync types"
  framing was wrong. The reason to still use an **overlay-owned opaque handle**
  (`OnboardCancel`/`OnboardCancelListener` on `tokio::sync::watch`) is cohesion + avoiding any
  Cargo.toml feature/dep edits and not relying on cross-crate feature unification for new code: the
  TUI merely holds the handle and `.cancel()`s it. (`tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken`, Option B,
  would still need tokio-util's `sync` feature — tui enables only `time` — i.e. extra feature edits.)
- **Fork tenets (codex CLAUDE.md):** minimize upstream-canonical conflict surface (prefer overlay
  edits; every upstream-canonical edit gets `// SANDBOX PATCH: remote_session` + a patch-surface
  row + a §15 rebase-replant note); resist adding dependencies; keep change < 800 lines; gate stays
  behind the existing `Feature::RemoteSession` (no new flag).

## Approach

### Architecture
Cooperative cancellation with an **overlay-owned cancel handle** built on `tokio::sync::watch`
(already available to codex-happy; race-free; dependency-free). The TUI holds the handle on the
`ChatWidget`, hands the listener half into the spawned `remote_on_flow`, and calls `.cancel()` on
`/remote off`. The overlay's poll loop selects on cancellation and returns `OnboardError::Cancelled`.

**Cancel-signal option matrix** (decision point for Phase-4 review):

| Option | Mechanism | New dep? | Hermetic abort test? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A (recommended)** | Overlay-owned `OnboardCancel`/`OnboardCancelListener` on `tokio::sync::watch` | None | Yes (overlay unit test) | Recommended — zero Cargo churn, cancellation logic stays in the overlay (conflict-surface-minimal), fully testable |
| B | `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` everywhere | Adds `tokio-util` to codex-happy **and** enables tokio-util's `sync` feature (tui enables only `time`) + Cargo.lock + `just bazel-lock-update` | Yes | Idiomatic but incurs the most Cargo/lock churn — feature/dep edits in two crates, which the fork tenets discourage |
| C | TUI-only `JoinHandle::abort()` (mirrors `thread_event_listener_tasks`), no overlay change | None | **No** — abrupt drop yields no `Cancelled` outcome/notice; abort-path test would be weak/racy | Rejected: operator explicitly wants a real abort-path test |

Recommended overlay API (final shape settled in impl/review):
```rust
// remote_on.rs (overlay, zero upstream surface)
pub struct OnboardCancel(tokio::sync::watch::Sender<bool>);            // TUI holds this
pub struct OnboardCancelListener(tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>); // passed into the flow
impl OnboardCancel {
    pub fn new() -> (Self, OnboardCancelListener) { /* watch::channel(false) */ }
    pub fn cancel(&self) { let _ = self.0.send(true); }               // &self; no Clone/Arc needed
}
// listener: is_cancelled() = *rx.borrow(); cancelled().await returns on send(true) OR sender-drop.
```
`poll_for_token` gains a `&mut OnboardCancelListener` param. **Use the minimal-restructure shape**
(it leaves the existing retry/return ladder untouched): add `if listener.is_cancelled() { return
Err(OnboardError::Cancelled); }` at the **top of each loop iteration**, and wrap **only** the
`tokio::time::sleep(...)` await (line 240 — the dominant multi-second wait) in
`tokio::select!{ _ = listener.cancelled() => return Err(OnboardError::Cancelled), _ = tokio::time::sleep(...) => {} }`.
Because `watch` is **level-triggered** (`*rx.borrow()` stays `true` once set), the top-of-loop check
plus the sleep-arm cancel together guarantee prompt cancellation (within the current HTTP round-trip
+ at the sleep) without restructuring the send/parse branches.

> **Do NOT wrap the whole send+parse+sleep iteration body in an inner `async { … }` inside
> `tokio::select!`.** `poll_for_token`'s body has several early `return Ok(...)`/`return Err(...)`
> statements (onboard.rs:201, 207-209, 212-214, 217-219, 224-228, 236-238); an inner `async` block
> would make those `return`s exit the *block*, not `poll_for_token`, silently breaking the
> `access_denied`/`expired_token`/deadline exits. The minimal shape above avoids this entirely. If a
> reviewer/impl prefers also cancelling during the in-flight HTTP `send().await`, wrap just that one
> await in its own `select!` arm too — never the whole branch ladder.

`run_self_onboard` gains an owned `OnboardCancelListener`, threads it (`&mut`) into `poll_for_token`,
and `is_cancelled()`-checks before the daemon/attach steps. On cancel it emits a cancellation notice
(`OnboardNotice::Progress("Onboarding cancelled.")`) through the sink **before** returning
`Err(OnboardError::Cancelled)` — so the overlay abort-path test asserts both the error AND the
surfaced cancellation notice hermetically (the feature request asks the abort-path test to assert a
cancellation notice).

### Implementation Strategy
1. **Overlay first (US-001):** `OnboardError::Cancelled` (+ `Display`), the `OnboardCancel`/listener
   types, cancel-aware `poll_for_token`/`run_self_onboard`, and the hermetic abort-path test. Lands
   independently (no upstream surface, fully unit-testable) — the smallest coherent first stage.
2. **TUI wiring + lifecycle + docs (US-002, depends on US-001's API):** `remote_on_cancel` field on
   `ChatWidget` (init `None`); `/remote on` **cancels any existing stored handle first** (explicit
   `.cancel()` before replacing — clearer than relying on watch sender-drop), then creates a fresh
   handle, stores it, and passes the listener into `remote_on_flow(tx, listener)`; `remote_on_flow`
   maps `Cancelled` → a clean info `RemoteSessionNotice`; `/remote off` calls `.cancel()` (in addition
   to the existing detach). **Lifecycle:** `App::replace_chat_widget`
   (`tui/src/app/session_lifecycle.rs:336`) currently transfers `remote_connection` to the replacement
   widget — add an analogous transfer of `remote_on_cancel` so an in-flight onboard stays cancellable
   across thread-switch/resume/fork. Fix the stale comment (815-821); extend the invariant test
   (`happy_seam_invariants.rs`, new `invariant_61`) to guard the new cancel seam; add the patch-surface
   invariant row + §15 rebase-replant note. Each new upstream-canonical seam/block gets an adjacent
   `// SANDBOX PATCH: remote_session` marker.

## Scope
### In Scope
- Prompt cancellation of an in-flight `/remote on` device-flow poll on `/remote off`.
- `OnboardError::Cancelled` + cancel-aware overlay onboard API + the abort-path test.
- Clean "onboarding cancelled" user notice mapping in `remote_on_flow`.
- Stale-comment cleanup (slash_dispatch.rs:815-821).
- Patch-surface invariant row + rebase-replant note.

### Out of Scope
- Any re-implementation of the already-shipped self-onboard, daemon supervision, or attach.
- New abort UX/keybindings beyond `/remote off` (e.g. Esc-to-cancel).
- Cancelling the daemon-bring-up/attach steps mid-flight (only a cheap pre-step `is_cancelled()`
  check is in scope; the poll is the long pole).
- Widget-**drop** / process-exit task cleanup (a `Drop` guard on the task) — out of scope; the task
  self-completes, is cancelled by `/remote off`, or is transferred across widget *replacement* (which
  IS in scope). The abandoned-on-process-exit case self-expires at `expires_in` as today.
- Migrating to `tokio-util::CancellationToken` (Option B) — documented but not chosen.

## Risk Areas
- **poll_for_token restructure (highest-risk edit):** the loop body has several early
  `return Ok(...)`/`return Err(...)` statements (onboard.rs:201, 207-209, 212-214, 217-219, 224-228,
  236-238). Do **not** wrap the whole iteration body in an inner `async { … }` inside `tokio::select!`
  — those `return`s would exit the inner block, not `poll_for_token`, silently breaking the
  `access_denied`/`expired_token`/deadline exits. Mitigation: use the minimal shape (top-of-loop
  `is_cancelled()` check + `select!` on the `sleep` await only), leaving the entire
  retry/backoff/return ladder untouched. An AC asserts the retry/backoff/deadline behavior is unchanged.
- **Widget replacement loses the handle:** `replace_chat_widget` builds a fresh `ChatWidget`; without
  transferring `remote_on_cancel` (as it already does for `remote_connection` at
  session_lifecycle.rs:336) an in-flight onboard becomes uncancellable from the replacement widget.
  Mitigation: add the transfer + an AC covering it.
- **watch sender-drop semantics:** `OnboardCancelListener::cancelled()` must return on **both**
  `send(true)` and sender-drop, so a second `/remote on` (which `.cancel()`s + replaces the stored
  handle) cancels the first in-flight onboard. The re-entry test verifies this.
- **Test determinism:** the abort-path test must reach the poll's await before cancelling. Approach:
  wiremock returns `authorization_pending` indefinitely (small `interval`), spawn `run_self_onboard`,
  wait until the sink has recorded the `DeviceCode` notice, then `cancel()`, then await the join
  inside `tokio::time::timeout(2s, …)` and assert `Err(Cancelled)` + cancellation notice + no
  `access.key`/`profile.json`. `watch` is level-triggered, so a `cancel()` that races ahead of the
  await still latches.
- **Stale handle after success:** after a successful onboard+attach the `remote_on_cancel` stays
  `Some` (the flow has no `&mut self`); a later `/remote off` (or a re-entrant `/remote on`)
  `.cancel()`s a finished listener — a harmless no-op (`watch::Sender::send` returns `Err` with no
  receivers, ignored). No `RemoteOnFinished` clear-event is needed.
- **Change size / conflict surface:** well under 800 lines; upstream-canonical surface limited to one
  struct field + the on/off handler edits + the one-line `replace_chat_widget` transfer, each marked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `OnboardError::Cancelled` variant exists with a `Display` arm; `cargo check -p codex-happy` passes.
- [ ] `poll_for_token` and `run_self_onboard` accept the cancel listener and return
      `Err(OnboardError::Cancelled)` when cancelled mid-poll, with the existing
      slow_down/authorization_pending/access_denied/expired_token/deadline behavior otherwise unchanged
      (the existing happy-path test still passes).
- [ ] `run_self_onboard` emits a cancellation `OnboardNotice` through the sink before returning
      `Err(Cancelled)`.
- [ ] New hermetic abort-path test in `remote_on_tests.rs`: drives `run_self_onboard` against a
      wiremock GitHub whose access-token endpoint returns `authorization_pending` indefinitely (small
      `interval`); after the `DeviceCode` notice is observed, `cancel()`s the handle; asserts —
      **within `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), join)`** (proving it does not wait for
      `expires_in`) — that the call returns `Err(OnboardError::Cancelled)`, surfaces the cancellation
      notice, and writes **no** `access.key`/`profile.json`. `cargo test -p codex-happy` passes.
- [ ] Re-entry test: dropping/replacing the `OnboardCancel` sender (or an explicit second `cancel()`)
      makes an in-flight `run_self_onboard` return `Err(OnboardError::Cancelled)` — covering the
      sender-drop-as-cancel semantics.
- [ ] `ChatWidget` has `remote_on_cancel: Option<OnboardCancel>` (init `None` in every constructor);
      `/remote on` `.cancel()`s any existing handle, then stores a fresh one and passes the listener
      into `remote_on_flow`; `/remote off` calls `.cancel()`.
- [ ] `App::replace_chat_widget` (session_lifecycle.rs) transfers `remote_on_cancel` to the
      replacement widget (mirroring `remote_connection`), so an in-flight onboard stays cancellable
      across thread-switch/resume/fork.
- [ ] `remote_on_flow` maps `OnboardError::Cancelled` to a clean info `RemoteSessionNotice` (not a
      diagnosed `remote_on_error`).
- [ ] The stale comment at slash_dispatch.rs:815-821 is corrected to state that `/remote on`
      self-onboards and is now cancellable.
- [ ] Every new upstream-canonical seam/block (the `remote_on_cancel` field, the `/remote on`
      cancel+store, the `/remote off` `.cancel()`, the `replace_chat_widget` transfer, the
      `remote_on_flow` listener param) carries an adjacent `// SANDBOX PATCH: remote_session` marker.
- [ ] `codex-rs-overlay/codex-invariant-tests/tests/happy_seam_invariants.rs` gains an `invariant_61_*`
      test asserting the new cancel seam markers; `cargo test -p codex-invariant-tests --test
      happy_seam_invariants` passes (existing 59/60 still pass).
- [ ] `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` has a new invariant row (id 61) + a §15 rebase-replant
      note documenting the cancel behavior and naming its enforcing tests.
- [ ] `cargo check --workspace` passes (Phase-5a gate) — run from `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs`.
- [ ] No new feature flag (gate remains `Feature::RemoteSession`); no new runtime dependency added to

- [ ] `just fmt` clean; `just fix -p codex-happy` / `just fix -p codex-tui` clean — run from

  remote_on.rs, remote_on_tests.rs): `OnboardError::Cancelled`, `OnboardCancel`/`OnboardCancelListener`,
  cancel-aware `poll_for_token` (top-of-loop check + sleep-select), `run_self_onboard` threads the
  listener + emits a cancellation notice, the timeout-bounded abort-path test + the re-entry test. No

  (chatwidget.rs, slash_dispatch.rs, app/session_lifecycle.rs, happy_seam_invariants.rs,

  comment fix, the `invariant_61` seam test, and the patch-surface row + §15 note. Depends on US-001's

## Open Questions
All four review-surfaced questions are now **resolved in the plan** (recorded here for the implementer):
- **Re-entry (`/remote on` while one is in flight):** `/remote on` explicitly `.cancel()`s the
  existing handle before replacing it (clearer than relying on watch sender-drop), and the re-entry
  test covers the sender-drop-as-cancel backstop. [RESOLVED]
- **Cancellation notice:** emitted from `run_self_onboard` through the sink, so the overlay abort-path
  test asserts it hermetically (no longer a TUI-only untested mapping). [RESOLVED]
- **Handle across widget replacement:** transferred in `replace_chat_widget` (mirroring
  `remote_connection`); an AC + the lifecycle risk cover it. [RESOLVED]
- **Cancel-signal mechanism:** Option A (overlay-owned `tokio::sync::watch` handle) — no Cargo/lock
  churn, cancellation cohesive in the overlay. Option B (tokio-util `CancellationToken`) documented but
  not chosen. [RESOLVED — default Option A per fork dep-minimization tenet.]
- **Remaining (non-blocking):** the impl member should confirm the exact `invariant_61` assertion
  shape against the current `happy_seam_invariants.rs` helpers (`section_between`, the
  `SLASH_DISPATCH_RS`/`CHATWIDGET_RS` consts).
